property_summary: For any deployment, the stored owner() getter of the contract returns the address set at initialization (the deployer in initialize), whereas the mutant returns address(0) breaking that equality for many inputs (e.g., any non-zero deployer); thus owner() should never be the zero address after initialize and must equal the initializer address.

After initialize(...) is called by an EOA X, owner() always returns that initializer address X (never address(0)); the mutant that forces owner() to return address(0) will violate this when initialized by any non-zero address.

After initialize(...) is called by some non-zero address A, owner() must return A (never address(0)); the mutant that forces owner() to always return address(0) will violate this for any non-zero initializer address.

After initialize(...) is called by any non-zero caller, owner() must return the initializer address (non-zero); the mutant that always returns address(0) will make owner() != initializer for some fuzzed initializer addresses.

After calling initialize(...) with any non-zero initializer address, owner() must NEVER be the zero address (it must equal the initializer); the mutant that unconditionally returns address(0) violates this for any non-zero initializer.
For any stored pause state, calling paused() returns that stored boolean; the mutant inverts the stored value so paused() != stored for some inputs.

For any boolean b written to the contract's paused state via pause()/unPause(), the public paused() getter returns the stored paused state (true if paused(), false if unpaused); the mutant inverts the returned value so for some sequence (pause or unPause) the getter's return differs.

For any address caller, after calling pause() or unPause() from the contract owner, the public paused() view must reflect the actual stored paused state (i.e. paused() == true right after pause(), paused() == false right after unPause()); the mutant that returns the inverted flag will cause this equality to fail for at least one fuzzed sequence (depending on which action was called).

For any sequence where the owner calls pause() or unPause(), the public paused() view must return the actual stored paused state (true after pause(), false after unPause()); the mutant that inverts the returned flag will make paused() disagree with the stored state for some fuzzed caller/action inputs.

For any caller that is the contract owner, after calling pause() the public paused() view returns true and after calling unPause() it returns false; the mutant inverts the returned flag so this rule is violated for some fuzzed inputs (depending which action is invoked).

For any tokenId when the contract is initialized, if no per-token royalty recipient is set (royalties[tokenId].royaltyRecipient == address(0)), getRoyalties MUST return the canonical default royaltyBPS of 500 and the initialized royaltyRecipient; the mutant returns 1000 instead, violating this rule for tokenIds without a per-token recipient.

For any tokenId when the contract has been initialized and no token-specific royalty recipient is set, getRoyalties MUST return the canonical default royaltyBPS of 500 (and the initialized royaltyRecipient); the mutant returns 1000 for those tokenIds, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any initialized C and any tokenId that has no token-specific royalty recipient set, getRoyalties(tokenId) must return royaltyBPS == 500 (the reference) — the mutant returns 1000 for such tokenIds, violating this rule for some inputs.
For any initialized C and any tokenId that has no token-specific royaltyRecipient set, getRoyalties(tokenId) MUST return royaltyBPS == 500 (reference) while the mutant returns 1000 for such tokenIds.

For any initialized C and any tokenId whose per-token royaltyRecipient is address(0), getRoyalties(tokenId) must return royaltyBPS == 500 (the reference); the mutant returns 1000 for such tokenIds, violating this rule for those inputs.

For any tokenId, calling getRoyalties on an uninitialized contract must revert (reference C requires initialization), whereas the mutant returns a default royalty instead of reverting for some tokenIds; thus the reference always reverts when not initialized but the mutant sometimes does not.
